Standard: The AR system has features to accomplish and maintain connection when mating systems are not aligned. a. Boom Tanker. The boom nozzle deflects angularly up to a 60-degree cone angle about the longitudinal axis of the boom and returns to within a 1-degree cone angle after deflection when the nozzle is not in contact with a receiver. The boom nozzle can rotate axially clockwise and counterclockwise at least 20 degrees and return to within 3 degrees of the 0-degree position after rotation when the nozzle is not in contact with a receiver. The nozzle has the capability to deflect and rotate and then return to neutral throughout the boom deployed envelope (airspeed, Mach, altitude, pitch, azimuth or roll, and boom wet (defined as 10 psig fuel pressure, which represents the worst-case fuel head pressure at maximum boom extension and lower elevation limit without fuel pumping pressure) or dry). b. Drogue Tanker. Reception coupling ball joint deflects within a 45-degree or greater cone angle and permits 360 degrees of axial rotation about the axial centerline of the coupling body. c. Receptacle Receiver. Receptacle bore axis installation angle enables alignment at contact with boom nozzle, in the center of the contact envelope, for all targeted tanker air vehicles. The receiver receptacle bore axis installation angle with respect to the receiver air vehicle waterline is calculated by using the following equation: 𝑋𝑋 = 30 − 𝐴𝐴 + 𝐵𝐵 2 + 𝐶𝐶 + 𝐷𝐷 2 A = maximum receiver air vehicle pitch angle B = minimum receiver air vehicle pitch angle C = maximum tanker air vehicle pitch angle D = minimum tanker air vehicle pitch angle d. Probe Receiver. Probe nozzle tip deflects up to 22.5 degrees off-center without damage and can deflect until the tip contacts the sliding sleeve lip, without breaking. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Examination of drawings verifies boom nozzle and ball joint design allows for 60 degrees of angular deflection and 20 degrees of rotation axially with appropriate components to facilitate a return to neutral position. b. Drogue Tanker. Examination of drawings verifies reception coupling ball joint design allows for required deflection and axial rotation. c. Receptacle Receiver. Examination of drawings and air vehicle calculated AOAs verifies receptacle installation angle adheres to required formula. d. Probe Receiver. Examination of drawings verifies probe nozzle design is capable of 22.5 degrees of deflection. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Laboratory testing verifies the boom nozzle can articulate in a 60-degree cone about the boom longitudinal axis. b. Drogue Tanker. Laboratory testing verifies the reception coupling deflects angularly to 45 degrees or greater and permits 360 degrees of axial rotation. c. Receptacle Receiver. Laboratory testing with targeted tanker boom nozzle and structure simulating the center of the contact envelope, verifies receptacle installation angle alignment. d. Probe Receiver. Laboratory testing verifies probe nozzle tip deflects up to 22.5 degrees without damage and deflects until the tip contacts the sliding sleeve lip, without breaking. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight testing with targeted receptacle-equipped receivers results in no damage, breakage, or inadvertent disconnects due to inability of the boom nozzle to articulate as needed. b. Drogue Tanker. Flight testing with targeted probe-equipped receivers results in no damage, breakage, or inadvertent disconnects due to inability of drogue coupling to articulate as needed. c. Receptacle Receiver. Flight testing with targeted boom-equipped tanker results in no damage, breakage, or inadvertent disconnects due to misalignment of the receptacle bore and boom centerline. d. Probe Receiver. Flight testing with targeted drogue-equipped tanker results in no damage, breakage, or inadvertent disconnects due to the inability of the probe nozzle tip to articulate as needed.
